title: Derived internal-Hom adjunction on a scheme
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let K, L, M be objects of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. Write K\otimes^L L for the derived tensor product, represented by \operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{O_X}\mathcal L^\bullet) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] for a K-flat complex \mathcal P^\bullet with a quasi-isomorphism \mathcal P^\bullet\to K [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a complex \mathcal L^\bullet representing L, and R\mathcal Hom for the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then there is a canonical bijection, functorial in K, L, and M, Hom_{D(O_X)}(K,R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\cong Hom_{D(O_X)}(K\otimes^L L,M). Moreover there is a canonical isomorphism K\otimes^L L\cong L\otimes^L K, functorial in K and L, so that also Hom_{D(O_X)}(K,R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\cong Hom_{D(O_X)}(L\otimes^L K,M), functorial in K, L, and M.

source.place: Cohomology Lemma cohomology-lemma-internal-hom (Tag 08DJ), equation (1) and proof; symmetry of the derived tensor product: Cohomology Lemma cohomology-lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived (Tag 0FPB)

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution P to K and a K-flat resolution L' to L by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and the K-injective resolution M to I fixed in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], which exists by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The category of sheaves of O_X-modules is symmetric monoidal with tensor-Hom adjunction by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed].

By [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] (with s the identity of I and t: L' to L), Hom^\bullet(L,I) to Hom^\bullet(L',I) is a quasi-isomorphism, and Hom^\bullet(L',I) is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]; so by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] Hom^\bullet(L',I) represents R Hom(L,M), and Hom^\bullet(P,Hom^\bullet(L',I)) represents R Hom(K,R Hom(L,M)) and is again K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. By [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] (Stacks Tag 0A8M) it is isomorphic as a complex to Hom^\bullet(Tot(P tensor L'),I), which represents R Hom(K tensor^L L,M) by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], since Tot(P tensor L') represents K tensor^L L ([def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], L' representing L). Taking H^0 of global sections of these isomorphic K-injective complexes and applying [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on both sides gives Hom_D(K,R Hom(L,M)) congruent to Hom_D(K tensor^L L,M).

source.place: Tag 08DJ proof and equation (1), using Tags 0A8M, 0A8T and 08JA

proof.text: Independence of the choices and functoriality in K, L, M: different K-flat resolutions of L and K-injective resolutions of M give quasi-isomorphic Hom complexes by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], all K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective], and the isomorphism of [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] and the identification of [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] are canonical and functorial; hence the bijection of Step 2 is canonical and functorial in K, L, and M.

The symmetry of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] on terms, with the Koszul sign (-1)^{pq} on P^p tensor L'^q, is an isomorphism of total complexes Tot(P tensor L') to Tot(L' tensor P) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] (a direct check against the total differential). Tot(P tensor L') represents K tensor^L L (P K-flat resolving K, L' representing L) and Tot(L' tensor P) represents L tensor^L K (L' K-flat resolving L, P representing K). Independence of the chosen resolutions: if A to B is a quasi-isomorphism and Q is K-flat, Tot(A tensor Q) to Tot(B tensor Q) is a quasi-isomorphism, since its cone is Tot(cone(A to B) tensor Q), acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex] (Stacks Tag 064K); comparing two choices through a common K-flat resolution [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] shows the isomorphism is canonical and functorial in K and L. Substituting it into Step 2 gives the final bijection.
